citations.field: PDF p.76; printed p.64; 八部 entry and continuation checked on PDF p.77
citations.text: The entry labels 八 a 指事字 and transmits the Shuowen interpretation that its strokes turn away from each other. It explains the graph as separating two strokes to express distinction, then says oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions also borrowed it as a numeral, citing “八羊” and a bronze date. The continuation check found no 八 text continuing on p.77; the 八 entry ends on p.76. This is the book's account, not independent proof that separation preceded numeral use.
